Hi Mark —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for inference at AtlasOne. Attaching a short mutual action plan and three technical stubs to get the access controls thread moving: SAML SP metadata (example), a suggested service-account pattern, and the MAP (high level).

Goal: schedule a 60-minute kickoff next week to align on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning cadence, IP allowlist windows, and service-account ownership for automation. Proposed agenda is at the top of the MAP.

Open items we want to confirm during kickoff:
- Desired SCT (short-term cutover) window and any blackout dates for IP changes
- Primary SSO contact + SAML cert rotation cadence
- SCIM attribute set required for entitlement mapping (name/email/groups/role)
- Service account model (ephemeral vs long-lived) and desired key rotation cadence

Can you confirm the right security contact and two preferred time windows? Ben will map any network constraints and Priyom will lead the SCIM/service-account work.

Attachments: AtlasOne_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_v1.pdf; SAML_SP_Metadata.xml; service-account-guidance.md

Thanks,

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the materials. We received the MAP and the SAML metadata example. A couple quick clarifications before confirming time:

1) IP allowlist expectations: are you expecting a /24 CIDR or a set of public IPs per region? We have a change freeze window on 2025-03-20 for a deployment, so anything that requires firewall changes before 2025-03-21 will be tight.

2) SCIM attributes: our identity team uses AD with group-to-role mappings; we generally only consume group membership and email. If SCIM needs name or department attributes for mapping, let us know.

Please loop in our security lead: AtlasOne Security <security@atlasone.com> (I’ll add Olga Simmons, our SSO engineer, to the thread after I check her schedule).

Best,

Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff: Access controls & IP cadence — AtlasOne mutual action plan

Mark — quick technical notes before we meet: 

- IPs: For the Hosted path we typically publish a small pool of egress IPs (not a /24) that you can allowlist. If you need region-specific endpoints we can provide separate IP sets per region. We will supply the exact list 48 hours before any required change window.

- SCIM: group membership + email is usually sufficient for entitlement mapping. If you plan to enforce department-level policies we can add department as an optional attribute; SCIM can be scoped to only publish specific attributes.

- Service accounts: we recommend ephemeral service accounts for private automation (short-lived tokens using KMS/HSM key wrapping) where possible; for integration with on-prem CI systems we can support rotated long-lived keys with a 90-day rotation policy. See attached guidance for patterns and examples.

I’ve attached service-account-guidance.md to this message for your engineers.

I’ll prepare a short network appendix and share it in the drive link prior to the meeting.

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
